subject: Human Evolution
title: The Expensive Tissue Hypothesis
description: Learn The Expensive Tissue Hypothesis in one minute.

hook.text: Brains and guts are both expensive to run. Leslie Aiello noticed they can't both be large at once.

buildup.text: Herbivores need long guts to extract nutrients from tough plants. That gut costs calories to maintain.

discovery.text: A meat-rich diet is easier to digest, needing a shorter gut—freeing energy for a bigger brain.

twist.text: The hypothesis is debated: some primates have both large guts and decent brains. It's not iron-clad.

climax.text: But the overall trend holds: as hominin diets improved in quality, brains grew and guts shrank.

punchline.text: Better food traded gut for brain.

quiz.question: What does the Expensive Tissue Hypothesis propose?
options: Higher-quality diets allowed smaller guts and larger brains
